findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in init workers
findings.body: searchSupport.init launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace. Inside the closure it does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where err is the outer variable from GetResourceStats. Multiple goroutines read/write the same err variable and increment the same int with no synchronization. This is a data race that corrupts the error return and the indexed count and will be flagged by -race. Use a local variable and return it, and use an atomic counter.

findings.title: Narrowed BuildIndex lock allows duplicate builds for same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the whole build, which serialized builds. It now only locks around b.cache[key] = idx. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both observe a miss, both call bleve.New on the same file directory and both run the builder, then last-writer-wins in the map. The loser index is leaked, IndexTenants metrics are double-incremented, and concurrent bleve.New on the same path can fail or corrupt the on-disk index. A per-key singleflight or double-checked lock is needed.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no RLock while BuildIndex concurrently does b.cache[key] = idx under Lock. Concurrent map read and write is a fatal data race in Go and can crash the process. It must hold cacheMu.RLock during iteration. The race window was widened by allowing concurrent builds.

findings.title: Watch loop uses Background context and ignores closed channel
findings.body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx := context.Background() and then loops with v := <-events followed by handleEvent(watchctx, v). If the storage WatchWriteEvents channel closes, the receive returns nil forever, causing a hot infinite loop and a nil-pointer dereference inside handleEvent when it accesses evt.Type. The Background context is also never cancelled, so polling queries are not tied to server shutdown. Derive the watch context from the server context and check the ok result of the receive.

findings.title: History/Origin panic when search is not configured
findings.body: Search checks if s.search == nil and returns an error, but History and Origin unconditionally call s.search.History and s.search.Origin. When Search.Resources is nil, newSearchSupport is skipped and s.search stays nil, so any History or Origin RPC causes a nil-pointer panic. Add the same nil guard as Search.

findings.title: Removing per-RPC Init checks removes stop gate
findings.body: All handlers previously called s.Init(ctx) which returned s.initErr, so after Stop set initErr to stopping/stopped, new Read/List/Create/Update/Delete/Watch/Search calls failed fast. After this change NewResourceServer calls Init once and handlers never consult initErr, so after Stop cancels the broadcaster context the server keeps serving reads and writes against the backend. Either re-check a stopped/failed flag per RPC or document that Stop no longer gates traffic.

findings.title: Silently skipping postgres storage-server test
findings.body: The test now skips when GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres with only a TODO comment. If eager Init at startup breaks postgres, this skip hides the regression and reduces coverage for exactly the backend this PR touches. The skip should be justified with a linked issue or removed before merge.
